concerns.text: Task T020 implements a 'Spatial Split' (Eastern US Train, Western US Test), directly violating Constitution Principle VII and Spec FR-004 which mandate a strict 'Temporal Split' (2015–2020 train, 2021 validate, 2022 test) to prevent circularity in phenology modeling.

Tasks T028 and T029 mandate implementing a Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM) and paired t-tests for statistical validation. This violates Spec FR-006 and US-3 Acceptance Scenario 1, which explicitly require a 'Diebold-Mariano test' to compare model performance.

Task T030 sets the sensitivity flag threshold at 'mean absolute difference > 3 days'. This contradicts Spec SC-003 and US-3 Acceptance Scenario 3, which define the failure flag threshold as 'variation in the median first-arrival date exceeds 7 days'.

Task T032 restricts visualization to the 'Continental US' while the Plan and Data Pipeline (T011-T015) are scoped to 'Lake Powell' (per Plan Summary). This creates a semantic drift where the task cannot deliver the Spec's FR-007 requirement for 'continental-scale maps' because the data scope is insufficient.

Task T012 specifies 'linear interpolation' for MODIS cloud gaps. While the Spec (Edge Cases) allows 'temporal interpolation', the Plan (Risks) explicitly mentions 'exclude weeks with > 50% cloud cover' as a mitigation. The task lacks the explicit constraint to exclude weeks with excessive gaps, risking data integrity if interpolation is applied to large missing blocks.
